a: Object storage keeps files as objects with keys in buckets (e.g. S3).
Presigned URLs grant time-limited upload/download without exposing credentials.
Modern S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for new objects.
Object storage often acts as origin for a CDN serving static assets.
Multipart upload splits large files into parts for reliability.
Storage classes trade cost vs access speed (hot, infrequent, archive).
Bucket policies define who can access objects at the bucket level.
Content-Disposition controls whether browsers display or download a file.
Scan user uploads asynchronously before making them public.
Signed cookies/URLs restrict CDN access to authorized users.
